title: Tanker Crashes Into Cruise Ship on the Mississippi
summary:
A giant tanker lost its steering on the Mississippi River on Friday and crashed into a docked river cruise ship in New Orleans. Everyone survived, but the crash left the cruise ship lying on its side and sent about 100 people into the river.

The tanker, the Atlantic Asphalt, is 520 feet long. It was heading to New Orleans when it appeared to lose steering, Coast Guard Captain Melanie Burnham said. The exact cause is not yet known. The ship blasted its horn several times as it floated toward the cruise ship, the American Heritage, which was finishing an eight-day cruise.

All 197 passengers and crew on the cruise ship survived, as did the tanker's crew. Thirty-two people were taken to hospital, including two police officers who were thrown into the river when the boat rolled. None of the injuries were critical, and eight people were still in hospital on Saturday.

Passengers were told to gather on the third deck and put on life vests. Then the ship suddenly rolled, sending passenger Joe Knab and about 100 others into the muddy river, where the water was 66 degrees Fahrenheit. Knab said he was in the water for about 15 minutes, and that it was a little scary at the time. Tugboats, other captains, nearby workers and police rushed to help.

The port of New Orleans has sued to make sure federal investigators can take control of the tanker, which it says caused at least 1 million dollars in damage to its terminal. A judge has given federal officials control of the ship for now. The National Transportation Safety Board has recovered the tanker's voyage data recorder and sent a 16-member team to investigate for a week. A first report is expected within 24 to 30 days. The tanker has been towed away, but moving the cruise ship could take weeks, and the first job is to remove its 16,000 gallons of fuel safely.
why_it_matters: A crash on a busy river can put hundreds of people in danger in minutes, and investigators need to find out why steering failed so it does not happen again.
